Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

visual adjective

also visually, visual arts, visual memory, to the eye

classical

Sen. Ep. 88.22: ad voluptātem oculōrum atque aurium (M-O s.v. art)
Gell. 2.26.3: in sēnsibus oculōrum

oculōrum

the genitive plural of oculus, beside the noun it describes, often set against aurium

of the eyes: visual

Classical Latin has no adjective for “visual”: it says “of the eyes”, as it says animī for mental (see mental). The visual arts are Seneca’s arts that aim ad voluptātem oculōrum (Morgan–Owens).

Other words

  • vīsūs — of sight, of seeing

    the genitive of vīsus, the sense of sight · also used · classical

    Where the sense itself is meant: vīsūs aciēs, keenness of sight (see vision).

  • vīsuālis, vīsuāle — visual, perceived by sight

    also used · late Latin · Cassiod. Var. 4.51: probātiō (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. art: artēs vīsuālēs

    Late Latin (Cassiodorus); Morgan–Owens gives it for the visual arts beside Seneca’s periphrasis.

Examples

  • erat in tantā cālīgine major ūsus aurium quam oculōrum

    in such thick fog the ears were of more use than the eyesLiv. 22.5.3

  • plūra … sunt … in sēnsibus oculōrum quam in verbīs vōcibusque colōrum discrīmina

    the eyes tell more colours apart than words and names canGell. 2.26.3

See also vision, see, mental, physical.
